nodes.label: Session.iter_poll
nodes.source_location: line 41: `Session.iter_poll(...)` accepts the same arguments as `poll` and yields one sample at a time, retaining no previous samples. Creating the iterator performs no I/O; validation and cancellation happen when it is consumed. `poll` collects that iterator into a list. Both bound a run to 10,000 samples; callers needing a stream should use the iterator and stop consuming or set the cancellation callback.

nodes.label: NegativeResponse
nodes.source_location: line 35: Clear codes, actuator tests, VIN writes, arbitrary UDS requests and programming are rejected before exchange. Positive responses must echo service plus `40`, PID and frame as applicable, with exact data lengths. Service `06` repeats MID in **each** nine-byte record; every echoed MID is checked. Fuel-trim parameters permit exactly one or two bytes where the standard allows a second bank; absence never becomes a zero-valued bank. Negative replies become `NegativeResponse(service, code)`; response-pending does not silently retry. Malformed/unrelated responses raise `DiagnosticError`. The backend reports a bounded no-response as `TimeoutError`. Health checks retain individual failures and continue sequentially; `Cancelled` always propagates. Cancellation is checked before and after exchange and cannot interrupt a blocking backend call.

nodes.label: Recorder
nodes.source_location: line 77: `Recorder(exchange)` exposes the same exchange method and saves accepted transactions with `save(path)`. It bounds storage and validates protocol responses. Saving uses exclusive creation so it cannot overwrite an existing recording. It records successful/negative exchanges, not timeout exceptions, raw USB packets, CAN frames or original Techstream TSE files. A recording containing VINs must be treated as vehicle data; the bundled authored example contains no real VIN.

nodes.label: Session.calibration
nodes.source_location: line 65: `Session.calibration(ecu)` is a separate read-only operation. It first reads `09 00` and queries `09 04` / `09 06` only when their support bits are set. The JSON-compatible result includes ECU, physical status, scope, status, errors and supported information types; successful fields are `calibration_ids` and `cvns`. Unsupported or failed fields are absent. This operation does not change the bundled health-check fixture or silently append extra requests.

nodes.label: Session.monitors
nodes.source_location: line 98: `Session.monitors(ecu)` walks the service `06` support maps and reads only advertised monitor IDs. It returns `supported_mids`, `results`, `status`, typed `errors`, provenance and physical status. Each nine-byte record is MID, TID, unit/scaling ID, then unsigned big-endian 16-bit value, minimum and maximum. The scaling ID selects signed two's-complement interpretation where defined. The supported scale inventory contains **all 92 defined IDs in SAE J1979-DA OCT2011 Annex E**; reserved/newer IDs remain `unresolved_scaling`, omit physical values and make the report `partial`. Numeric conversion uses the published scaling/bit column, not rounded extrema in examples. Units are preserved explicitly, including milliamperes, microseconds and inches where defined.

nodes.label: SAE J1979
nodes.source_location: line 67: CAN information responses require a nonzero record count followed by exactly that many records: 16 bytes per CALID and four bytes per CVN. CALIDs accept printable ASCII with trailing NUL padding only. CVNs preserve all four bytes as eight uppercase hex digits, including leading zeros. These representations follow SAE J1979 MAY2007 §6.10 and Annex G tables G4/G6; [the 2002 incorporated standard](https://law.resource.org/pub/us/cfr/ibr/005/sae.j1979.2002.pdf) also defines the CALID/CVN fields. Arrays remain independent; the module does not invent a manufacturer-specific mapping between IDs and checksums. Reading a CVN neither calculates one locally nor certifies software authenticity. A response-pending NRC remains an explicit error; no unbounded wait is added.

line 67: CAN information responses require a nonzero record count followed by exactly that many records: 16 bytes per CALID and four bytes per CVN. CALIDs accept printable ASCII with trailing NUL padding only. CVNs preserve all four bytes as eight uppercase hex digits, including leading zeros. These representations follow SAE J1979 MAY2007 §6.10 and Annex G tables G4/G6; [the 2002 incorporated standard](https://law.resource.org/pub/us/cfr/ibr/005/sae.j1979.2002.pdf) also defines the CALID/CVN fields. Arrays remain independent; the module does not invent a manufacturer-specific mapping between IDs and checksums. Reading a CVN neither calculates one locally nor certifies software authenticity. A response-pending NRC remains an explicit error; no unbounded wait is added.

line 135: The monitor record layout/support chain and zero-results rule come from [SAE J1979 APR2002, §6.6](https://s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/ptab-filings%2FIPR2023-00504%2F1075). Scale/configuration/information definitions use [SAE J1979-DA OCT2011, Annexes B/E/G](https://www.e90post.com/forums/attachment.php?attachmentid=1509324&d=1476497126). Later scalar quantities were cross-checked against the [instrument manufacturer's machine-readable PID data](https://canlogger.csselectronics.com/files/misc/obd2-pid-table-service-01.csv). These are standard definitions, independent of a claim that a specific Toyota implements them.
